startup.name: AgentPhone
startup.description: An API that gives each AI agent its own phone number for calls and messages so it can reach people and businesses. Customers are developers and companies building agents; pricing is likely usage-based on numbers, minutes and messages, resold over carrier networks. Team size not stated.

yc_acceptance.basis: Start from about 1 percent. Adjust up for a clear developer-facing wedge in agent infrastructure and fast-growing demand for voice and messaging agents; adjust down because it is a thin layer on top of carriers such as Twilio and Telnyx, there is no stated team background or traction, and voice infrastructure is crowded (Vapi, Bland, Retell, Surge). Net about 2 percent; already in the Spring 2026 batch.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say this is a wrapper over existing telephony APIs: Twilio, Telnyx and the voice-agent platforms already provide numbers, and the one-liner does not say what is hard that they cannot add in a quarter. The team size and background are not stated, and carrier registration and spam rules could swallow a small team.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2026 gave seed 36% lower / 44% known / 54% upper, cond 44% (n=1541); series_a cond 20% (n=679); series_b cond 19% (n=136); series_c cond 19% (n=26). Calibration-only B2B: seed 52/65/72, series_a cond 32%, series_b cond 46%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 7.4 months (2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17); seed means an outside round above about $1M closing in it. Anchor 0.44 ever for B2B 2022+ with median 6 months to seed and p25 3, so about 70 to 80 percent of ever-seeds close in 7 months; I lift to 0.45, within the 1.25x cap, for the strength of the agent-infrastructure theme and the voice-AI analogs Vapi, Bland AI and Retell AI that raised early, offset by an unknown team. The odds do not rank the company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels and a seed fund, the thin band. Cohort B2B 2022+ seed raise p25 is $2.0M, so about a third of rounds land here; the YC deal alone (about $500K) does not count as seed in this window.
Typical institutional seed. Cohort median is $3.3M to $4.0M (B2B 2022+, n=530) and the winners test confirmed raises had quartiles of $4.3M and $10M, so this band holds the middle.
Hot-category seed led by a known fund. In the winners test 42 percent of confirmed raises fell in $6M to $12M, though press coverage biases that sample upward, so it is weighted below that.
Upside band: a large AI-category seed or pivot-then-raise path with top-tier lead. Rare in the cohort (above the p75 of $5.0M to $6.0M by 2x).

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed fails if usage does not show quickly: investors need agent developers actually paying for numbers, and carriers and CPaaS firms can undercut price. Surge (F24, Stripe for telephony) and Struct (W23, shut down) show voice infrastructure can stall without a round, and unit margins on resold minutes are thin, so a small founding team may not reach the traction investors want in 7 months.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2026: series_a cond 20% (n=679); time table months_to_series_a p50 28, p25 19 (era 2022+).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 7.4 months, and Series A p25 is 19 months after batch start in the 2022+ time table, so only a small share of the 0.20 ever anchor falls in the window. Used 0.06, the discount being for time and not for company quality. Vapi and Bland did reach later rounds quickly, which keeps it above 0.04.

bands.rationale: Thin or flat-ish Series A on modest ARR; the 2018-2021 B2B series_a p25 was $10M, so this is below the typical cohort round and covers extension-like A rounds.
Central case. B2B 2022+ series_a raise p25 $13M, median $17M, p75 $22M (n=130); post-money reported for only n=3 so valuation is thin data.
Upside band with fast ARR growth in a hot AI category; 2022+ all-industry series_a post-money p75 was $345M on n=18 reported rounds.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A needs usage-based revenue of about $1M to $2M ARR with healthy gross margins. A reseller of carrier capacity has thin margins and customers can switch to Twilio or Telnyx, so growth must come from agent-specific features like identity, compliance and memory, which need time to prove.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2026: series_b cond 19% (n=136); calibration-only B2B cond 46% (n=61); lower/known/upper ranges 1/2/19 percent ever.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Anchor cond 19 percent; 0.20 because voice AI analogs Vapi (series B) and Bland AI (later rounds) show faster progress than the typical B2B cohort in this wave.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B below the cohort p25 of $39M, flat or modest step up.
Central: B2B 2022+ series_b median $42.5M raise and $600M post (n=9 valuations).
Upside band for a category leader; era is inflated by AI rounds so use with care.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B requires the company to become the default identity and messaging layer for agents, with large enterprise accounts. Twilio, Telnyx and agent platforms can bundle numbers, and carriers control pricing, so growth may stall at a niche developer audience, as Surge (F24) and Vogent (S21) show for telephony infrastructure that never became the default.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2026: series_c cond 19% (n=26); calibration-only B2B cond 50% (n=28).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Anchor cond 19 percent; 0.15 because a telephony reseller faces margin pressure and few YC analogs reached a Series C (Bland is the exception).

bands.rationale: Modest growth round; series_c 2022+ p25 raise $50M.
Central: 2022+ series_c median raise $74M to $101M, post-money median about $1.2B (n=3 to 34).
Upside: breakout category winner, cf. Bland-style rounds; very few companies.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C needs hundreds of millions in volume. Voice infrastructure has capital-heavy competitors and carrier relationships that are hard to replicate, and acquirers such as Twilio or the model labs may buy the category instead of letting an independent scale; Vocode and Vogent ended as acquisitions rather than as independent growth stories.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likeliest outcome is a small acquisition by a CPaaS or voice platform, as happened to Vocode and Vogent, or a stall as agent builders consolidate on the voice platforms. A $1B outcome requires agent identity to become a standard layer, and carriers or labs may build it.

killers.risk: Carrier and CPaaS incumbents (Twilio, Telnyx) add agent features and undercut price.
killers.evidence: Telnyx and Twilio already expose numbers, SMS and voice APIs that agents can call.
killers.mitigation: Offer agent-native identity, compliance and memory, not raw numbers.

killers.risk: Regulation and spam: carrier registration, 10DLC rules and anti-robocall enforcement can block agent-initiated calls.
killers.evidence: Production SMS and outbound calls need registration and consent, and agents risk number blacklisting.
killers.mitigation: Build compliance into the product and screen customers.

killers.risk: Thin gross margins from reselling carrier minutes.
killers.evidence: Resold voice minutes and SMS carry carrier costs that leave small margins at low volume.
killers.mitigation: Add software value and sell platform fees on top of usage.

killers.risk: Voice-agent platforms bundle numbers so customers never buy separately.
killers.evidence: Vapi, Bland and Retell AI already attach numbers to their agent products.
killers.mitigation: Be the neutral layer that works across all agent platforms.

technical_complexity.rationale: Provisioning numbers and routing calls and messages through carrier partners is not hard in 3 months; the hard parts are carrier registration, compliance, call quality and reliability, and fraud prevention, which a small team can reach with partners but cannot own.

takeover_risk.rationale: A CPaaS can ship an agent-numbers product in a few months and already has the carrier relationships and customers; platform dependency on carriers also limits pricing power.

evidence.claim: Several startups already offer phone numbers and SMS for AI agents, which shows developer demand.
Carrier APIs are marketing agent use cases, a sign of spend.

actions: Add compliance and registration so customers can go to production

pros.point: Clear, simple developer wedge and timely agent theme.
pros.evidence: One-liner states a single product, numbers for agents.

pros.evidence: Vapi and Bland AI reached series B and C in the researched records.

brand.name: AgentPhone
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "AgentPhone" --era 2022+: 10 chars, 2 words, compound words.
weaknesses: Generic compound name, hard to defend and to rank in search
Other agent phone products use close names
brand.rationale: A descriptive compound is clear like Surge-style category names but is easy to copy and weak as a brand; several competitors use nearby names, so it neither helps nor hurts the odds much.

narrative.headline: A clear, timely agent infrastructure wedge, but a thin reseller layer over carriers with strong incumbents.
narrative.general_summary: AgentPhone sells phone numbers to AI agents. Demand from agent builders is plausible and voice-AI neighbors Vapi and Bland AI raised sizeable rounds in the previous wave, but the layer sits on top of carriers and CPaaS vendors that can add the same feature, and Struct and Surge show that voice infrastructure can stall. Over a 7.4 month window the cohort anchor for a seed above $1M is about 0.44 ever and most of it falls in the first 6 months; I use 0.45. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Window is 7.4 months from 2026-04-06; seed means an outside round above about $1M.
Team size is not stated in the input, so no team-based adjustment was made.

Competitors in the list come from non-AgentPhone search results (Telnyx, Firsty, Tryvox).
